title: Brown Butter Chocolate Steel-Cut Oatmeal
changes_from_base: Steel-cut oats are fried in browned butter, then simmered in cocoa-darkened water for a chocolatey porridge, sweetened to taste and finished with cream, banana, dates, coconut and flaky salt.
summary: Earthy chocolate and nutty brown butter provide unexpected depth to steel-cut oats, finished with cool cream and scattered fruit for a sophisticated breakfast.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
maple syrup or honey, to taste

steps.title: Brown butter
steps.text: Melt 28 g butter in a large saucepan over medium heat and cook, swirling, 2-4 min until deep golden and nutty (the bubbling quietens when close).

steps.title: Toast oats
steps.text: Add 265 g steel-cut oats and fry 2-4 min until golden at the edges.

steps.title: Water and cocoa
steps.text: Scrape the oats and butter into a heatproof bowl, bring 1080 ml water to the boil in the same pan, whisk in 3 tbsp cocoa until smooth, then whisk in the buttered oats and ¼ tsp salt.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Simmer gently 25-30 min, stirring now and then.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Off the heat, cover and rest 5 min; thin with boiling water if too thick.

steps.title: Sweeten and serve
steps.text: Sweeten with 3 tbsp maple syrup or honey to taste, then top each bowl with 60 ml single cream or milk, sliced banana, sliced dates, 2 tbsp desiccated coconut and ¼ tsp flaky sea salt.

tips: Listen for the butter's bubbling to quiet down; that indicates it has browned enough.
Save the brown butter solids in the oats; don't strain them out, as they add flavour.
Dates add natural sweetness and chewy texture that complements chocolate beautifully.
storage: Serve hot; leftover porridge keeps in the fridge for 2 days and reheats gently with extra boiling water. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
